subject: How are the size of points created in geom_point

messages.author: a0e82b98c8b5b862
messages.subject: How are the size of points created in geom_point
parts:
I have been working on an optimum experimental design problem where I am trying to find the proportion of units I should allocate to 4 different factor-level combination of temperature and current.  The following code shows one way that I have been trying to show such an optimum plan:

library(ggplot2)

o.pts <- data.frame(Temp = c(40,93,40,93),Current = c(30,30,40,40),
                    prop = c(0.4873989, 0.1435308, 0.1226544, 0.2464159 ))
p <- ggplot(o.pts,aes(Temp,Current,size = prop))
p + geom_point() + scale_size(name = "Proportion",
                   breaks = sort(c(0.4873989, 0.1435308, 0.1226544, 0.2464159 ),decreasing = T),
                   labels = sort(c(0.487, 0.144, 0.123,0.246),decreasing = T) ) +
                   xlab("Ambient Temperature (Degrees C)") + ylab("Current (milliAmps)")+
                   theme_bw() +
    opts(axis.text.y = theme_text(size = 12,hjust = 1)) +
    opts(axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 15,angle = 90)) +
    opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(size = 12,vjust = 1)) +
    opts(axis.title.x = theme_text(size = 15)) 

where Temp is for temperature, Current is for current, and prop is the proportion of units.  My question is what is the relation between the size of the points plotted and the values of prop set in the aesthetic?  Naively in my write up I was saying that the area of the points is proportional to the proportion allocated but I do not believe this to be true.  Thank you for your help in advance.

Brian

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: How are the size of points created in geom_point
parts:
Hi,

geom_point (i.e., pointsGrob in grid package) draw symbols as characters.
And size aes is finally used for fontsize specification (see ?pointsGrob).
So it is hard to say the relation between size value and actual size
of symbols, but probably, in the case of circle symbol, the size
corresponds to the radius.

try this:

d <- data.frame(x=c(1,1,2,2),y=c(1,2,1,2),s=c(1,2,3,4)*10)
ggplot(d, aes(x,y,size=s)) + geom_point() + scale_size_identity() +
xlim(0,3) + ylim(0,3)
